title: Bribery step using a maximum-influence coordinate
statement: Let $n\ge 2$, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be monotone, and let $J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. Suppose the mean of the function obtained by setting all coordinates in $J$ to $1$ lies in $[-99/100,99/100)$. Choose a coordinate $i$ of maximum influence for that modified function. Then $i\notin J$, and setting the coordinates in $J\cup\{i\}$ to $1$ increases the mean by at least $199\log(n)/(1{,}000{,}000n)$.
